name: Clarisonic

card.summary: Clarisonic was a line of oscillating sonic facial-cleansing brushes, used to wash the face more thoroughly in support of clearer-looking skin.
card.aka: Clarisonic Mia, Alpha Fit, Mia Fit
card.note: The brand was discontinued by L'Oreal in 2020; used units remain in circulation.

quick.overview:
Clarisonic was a brand of handheld facial-cleansing brushes with a brush head that oscillates at sonic speeds. People used it with a cleanser to wash the face more thoroughly than by hand, with the aim of cleaner, clearer-looking skin.

The first device launched in 2004 from Pacific Bioscience Laboratories of Redmond, Washington, and L'Oreal acquired the company in 2011. By 2018 Clarisonic held about 14% of the skin care device market, and L'Oreal announced the brand's discontinuation in July 2020.
quick.how: Users wet the face, apply a cleanser to the brush head or skin, and move the oscillating head over each area of the face as part of a morning or evening routine. Models included the Mia 2 with two speeds, the Alpha Fit for men and the compact Mia Fit. Replacement brush heads were sold separately.
quick.risks: As with any mechanical cleansing, people with sensitive or inflamed skin may find brushing irritating, and brush heads are a replaceable part. No published clinical trial of the brand has been identified.

lead: Clarisonic was a line of battery-powered facial-cleansing brushes whose heads oscillate at sonic speeds. They were used alongside a cleanser to remove oil, makeup and debris, supporting a clearer complexion and better absorption of skincare, the chain people cited for using it to look better [1].

The brand came from Pacific Bioscience Laboratories, founded in Redmond, Washington, in 2001 by David Giuliani, Robb Akridge, Steve Meginniss, Ward Harris and Ken Pilcher. Giuliani had earlier co-founded Optiva, maker of the Sonicare toothbrush, and Pilcher is credited as lead inventor of the skincare systems [1].

L'Oreal bought the company in 2011 and announced in July 2020 that it would discontinue the brand to focus on other core offerings [1]. In bodybuilding forums, users mention using a Clarisonic with a cleanser to manage skin breakouts during steroid cycles [2].

chain: Oscillating brush head loosens oil, makeup and debris
Face is cleansed more thoroughly than by hand
angle.text: The device is a cleansing tool: it works the cleanser across the skin to leave the face cleaner. People use it as part of an acne or general skincare routine to keep their complexion looking clear.

infobox: Mia 1 and 2, Alpha Fit (men), Mia Fit [1]

paras: The Clarisonic system combined a handle with a rechargeable motor and interchangeable round brush heads that oscillate rapidly. The first model, later called the Mia 1, launched in 2004 [1]. The Mia 2 (2012) offered two oscillation speeds, the Alpha Fit (2015) was aimed at men, and the compact Mia Fit followed in 2016 [1].

Pacific Bioscience Laboratories was founded in 2001 by five people including Sonicare co-founder David Giuliani and inventor Ken Pilcher, whose earlier work included avionics for the NASA Space Shuttle [1]. L'Oreal acquired the brand and parent in 2011 [1].

In September 2016 L'Oreal cut 120 jobs in Redmond and began outsourcing production [1]. In 2018 Clarisonic accounted for 14% of the skincare device market, and the discontinuation announced in July 2020 was attributed by the company to a focus on other core businesses, with observers speculating that cheaper competitors played a part [1].
On T Nation, one poster describes washing the face twice daily with an antibacterial wash and a partner's Clarisonic and cleanser to limit acne while on anabolic compounds [2].
